title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying a category P of 'Σ-perfect' chain-complex-like objects L. (equivalently, finite chain complexes in which the L_i, Z_i, B_i and H_i are free of finite type). Σ is the class of 'Σ-exact' short sequences, meaning the sequences of L_i, Z_i, B_i and H_i are all exact (split-exact). This sets up a relative homological algebra in which the Σ-projectives and Σ-injectives are generated by the contractible objects C^i (and Ψ^0); this is used on the next page.

The page is a 'Remarque' on the categorical status of (P, Σ). Points made:
1. The category admits kernels and cokernels but is not abelian: a bimorphism need not be an isomorphism.
2. If N is the kernel of A → B, then N → A is a Σ-mono (admissible monomorphism). It therefore sits in a Σ-exact sequence N → A → A' → 0.
3. The induced map A' → B is in general NOT a Σ-mono. So morphisms are not 'strict' with respect to Σ, and (P, Σ) does not behave like an abelian category with its usual exact sequences.

He then starts, and repeatedly crosses out, an axiomatisation of the situation. The sketch is a category B together with a full subcategory C' (the Σ-injectives or projectives) and a class Σ_C of exact sequences, such that:
- every morphism A → B of B admits a kernel K with K → A a Σ_C-mono;
- possibly, stability of the distinguished objects under B-extensions.
He also contemplates a functor transforming C' into C' and preserving Σ-exact sequences.

The aim is to justify the standard relative-homological-algebra statements used on the next page: Σ-injective right resolutions exist and are unique up to homotopy, with a unique homotopy class of comparison maps, and dually for projectives. In modern terms this is an attempt to isolate the axioms of an exact (Quillen) or pre-abelian/quasi-abelian category with enough relative injectives and projectives.
errors: Existence of kernels in the category of complexes with free f.g. L_i, Z_i, B_i, H_i is asserted, not proved. Over a non-field ring, the degreewise kernel can have non-free homology, so the categorical kernel needs an argument; the previous page only proves it under a surjectivity hypothesis.
The axiomatisation is left unfinished: heavily crossed out, with no final list of axioms.

ideas.what: Category with a distinguished class Σ of short exact sequences (split on L, Z, B, H) used for relative homological algebra
ideas.modern_name: Exact category / proper class of exact sequences; relative homological algebra

ideas.what: Observation that the category is additive with kernels and cokernels but not abelian (bimorphisms not isos), with the coimage→image map not admissible
Axioms ensuring every morphism has a kernel that is an admissible mono, aimed at uniqueness up to homotopy of relative injective/projective resolutions
ideas.modern_name: Comparison theorem in relative homological algebra / exact categories with enough injectives
ideas.usually_credited_to: Eilenberg–Moore 1965; Bühler's survey of exact categories

deep.surprise_reason: This is a side remark checking standard relative homological algebra and exact-category axioms for a specific category of complexes. The content is well known (Eilenberg–Moore, Quillen), and the attempted axiomatisation is abandoned.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'la catégorie P ≃ P. admet des Σ-noyaux (et des conoyaux, mais un bimorphisme n'est pas nécessairement un iso)'.
Around line 6: 'Il est vrai que si N est le noyau de A → B, alors N → A est un Σ-mono, se plonge dans une suite Σ-exacte N → A → A' → 0, mais'.
Line 'A' → B n'est pas en général un Σ-mono' is correctly read.

The bottom section mentions 'Σ_C des suites exactes' and 'tout morphisme A → B de B admette un noyau K tel que K → A soit un Σ_C-mono'. The final parenthesis seems to end with 'qui transforme C' en C' et qui ... les Σ-exactes ... e.g.'
